subject.title: Durable core PR2/6: add optional shared-state foundation

question: Should OpenClaw adopt an opt-in shared durable-runtime schema and configuration boundary now, or require each cross-owner durability gap to remain with its existing owner-specific subsystem?
rationale: The branch introduces a new core persisted-state owner and public configuration contract; choosing whether that layer should exist is a product and architecture decision that cannot be safely inferred from store-level tests.

options.title: Pause for RFC decision
options.body: Keep this implementation pending until maintainers accept, narrow, or reject the owner-first residual boundary in the linked RFC.

options.title: Sponsor a reduced foundation
options.body: Approve a tightly scoped shared-state seam, remove inactive worker and retention controls, and require fresh-install and upgrade behavior proof before merge.

options.title: Keep owner-specific durability
options.body: Reject the generic layer and address verified cross-owner gaps through the current task, flow, subagent, delivery, and session owners.

recommendation.title: Pause for RFC decision
recommendation.body: Keep this implementation pending until maintainers accept, narrow, or reject the owner-first residual boundary in the linked RFC.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored both the RFC and this implementation slice and can clarify or narrow the proposed boundary for maintainer review.
